name: Georgia

regulator.name: Georgia Secretary of State, Professional Licensing Boards (Athlete Agents)

covers_nil_agents: Probably. The act covers endorsement contracts (paid use of an athlete's fame), but it never says NIL by name.
contract_warning: Warning to student athlete if you sign this contract: (1) you may lose your eligibility to compete as a student athlete in your sport; (2) if you have an athletic director, within 72 hours after entering into this contract, both you and your athlete agent must notify your athletic director; and (3) you may cancel this contract within 14 days after signing it. Cancellation of this contract may not reinstate your eligibility.
summary: Register with the Secretary of State. $210 plus a $10,000 surety bond.

steps.text: Fill out the Athlete Agent initial application
steps.detail: Finish the whole file within 6 months of your first document.
From a surety allowed in Georgia. Keep it active the whole time you're registered.
An affidavit or certificate in contracts, negotiation, complaint resolution, arbitration or contract disputes.

steps.text: Attach ID, character affidavits and any court records
steps.detail: Notarized character affidavits. Out-of-state agents also file a notarized service-of-process designation.

steps.text: Mail everything to Georgia Athlete Agent
Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Your pay and how it's figured, any other pay you get, anyone else being paid, expenses, services, length and date signed.

steps.text: Put the warning in bold capital letters near the athlete's signature
steps.detail: Use the exact words Georgia gives.

steps.text: Give the athlete a copy when they sign
Notify the athletic director in writing within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, whichever comes first. The athlete may cancel within 14 days.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: State law and federal law (SPARTA) both ban pre-dating or post-dating it.
Names and addresses, contracts and recruiting costs. The Secretary of State can inspect them.

steps.text: Never lie or make false promises to sign an athlete
steps.detail: Don't give the athlete anything of value before they sign. Don't give anything to anyone else, like a coach, except another registered agent.

steps.text: Renew by June 30 of each odd year and keep the bond active

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: Georgia's athlete agent law was read on Justia (2025 code) and FindLaw (current to March 2024), not the official code. Confirm 43-4A-13 to 43-4A-15 on the official code at law.lexisnexis.com/gacode.
Georgia repealed its college NIL law (O.C.G.A. 20-3-680 to 20-3-683) on July 1, 2025. Ask the Secretary of State's athlete agent board whether NIL-only agents must register.
